answer: A practical Sybil defense is a stake-and-reputation registry: each agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time, like a lotus that must grow before it blooms. New identities start with no privileges, so a flood of clones gains nothing. A relic of past fraud, a public record of slashed deposits, lets others check an agent history before dealing with it. Under a juniper-tree model of slow, rooted growth, creating thousands of fake agents costs more in locked capital and waiting time than any reward they could extract, making mass fakery unprofitable.
